title: Arthur Rimbaud's birth chart
metaDescription: Arthur Rimbaud's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 26.8° Libra. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a sextile: Mercury and Jupiter within 0.7°, thinking wired to expansion. A sixth of the circle is close enough for cooperation and far enough that it stays optional.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 26.8° Libra — the third decan, 20°–30°, which the tradition sub-rules by Mercury. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Libra and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Scorpio (19.1°), Venus in Libra (13.4°), Mars in Sagittarius (7.0°): a mind that absorbs before it argues, taste led by wit and proportion, drive that ignites on contact.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: Mercury to Jupiter, a sextile with 0.7° of slack. A sixth of the circle is close enough for cooperation and far enough that it stays optional. Behind it, Uranus sextile Neptune at 1.9°, and Saturn square Neptune at 1.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, three sit in a sign it has an opinion about. The Sun in Libra at 26.8° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Venus in Libra at 13.4° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Capricorn at 19.8° is in fall. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Tallied where the signs are certain — 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day — the chart gives air 4, earth 3, water 2, fire 1, and cardinal 4, fixed 3, mutable 3 across the modes. Saturn, Uranus, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Libra for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.1° between midnight and midnight. Whatever the unrecorded hour was, it happened inside one Moon sign — the degree floats, the sign holds. At the noon reference it stands at 9.5°.
